Most likely it's not that these people have a 100% negative view of parenting; it's more that the internet is their only outlet for the negative aspects of parenting. It's considered extremely inappropriate to respond to "How is being a parent?" with anything other that "I absolutely love every second of it and never regret it, even for a moment!" in real life. The culture (and sometimes anonymity) of the internet allows people to be truly honest with their feelings, so the people with mixed feelings take the opportunity to dump all of their negative ones, and the result is that the internet ends up being skewed negative, the way real life ends up being skewed positive about it.

But that's my point - I don't have those negative feelings. I truly don't. So when people tell me I'm suppose to, or I'm not "paying my dues" until I do, I'm confused. All the stuff they complain about isn't as terrible as they make it out to be (in my world).

It's similar to all the people who go about claiming that marriage is hard and how it is so much work. It isn't either one of those really. Yeah there is some work, but it is enjoyable work - do what you love and you never work a day. The hardest part is overcoming your own ego. Once you get your head out of your ass it is not hard at all. I understand that there are people in rough marriage and extenuating circumstances, but a couple middle age yuppies in a non-violent marriage are the last people who should be saying marriage is hard. Not surprisingly this same group has significant overlap with the parent bloggers OP is talking about.

The internet is probably the only place the people you are sick of are able to be truthful. When they're taking the kid to daycare or swimming lessons, they have to pretend to be enjoying themselves and they need to talk to other parents about how "It's so wonderful and rewarding being a parent, even though I'm tired, teehee" If you want to associate with parents who like being parents, then why not create a Positive Parenting community?
